skill.name: MapReduce Skill
skill.description: Coordinates parallel AI workers and external providers, then compares or consolidates their outputs using documented workflows and scoring rubrics.
skill.summary: Fan out planning, implementation, or debugging tasks and reduce multiple results into one attributed outcome.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Manual review found that most alerts are Markdown wording or deterministic shell examples, but four command-substitution examples invoke external AI CLIs and create data-disclosure or workspace-change risks. Additional review found that generated implementations may be executed during reduction and optional cleanup can irreversibly delete artifacts; no prompt injection language was present.

remediation.issue: External provider examples send prompts or local specification content to third-party CLIs, and Codex examples enable full-auto mode.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, redact sensitive content, avoid full-auto mode, and document each provider's data handling before invocation.

remediation.issue: The reduction workflow can run tests against AI-generated implementations.
remediation.suggestion: Review generated code first, then compile and test it inside an isolated environment without secrets, network access, or host write permissions.

remediation.issue: The optional cleanup example uses recursive deletion with wildcards.
remediation.suggestion: Archive files by default and require a dry run plus explicit confirmation before deleting matched paths.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md lacks valid frontmatter and was excluded from static scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Add valid marketplace frontmatter so future static scans cover the entry file.

content.user_title: Coordinate Parallel AI Work with MapReduce
content.value_statement: Complex tasks benefit from independent perspectives, but comparing results manually takes time. This skill coordinates parallel workers and consolidates their outputs with structured rubrics.
actual_capabilities: Defines map, collect, and reduce phases for parallel AI work.
Provides examples for Claude subagents and Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode CLIs.
Organizes plans, implementations, diagnoses, reviews, and consolidated artifacts with consistent names.
Compares generated implementations using correctness, readability, maintainability, performance, and security criteria.
Consolidates competing plans with attribution, confidence levels, conflict notes, and weighted priorities.
limitations: This package provides documentation and templates, not an executable orchestration runtime.
External CLI examples require installed tools, authentication, and approval before project content leaves the environment.
Referenced reducer definitions and the debug consensus cookbook are not included in this package.
Consensus and rubric scores do not replace manual security, correctness, or architecture review.

use_cases.title: Compare Architecture Plans
use_cases.description: Generate conservative, aggressive, security, and scalability plans, then combine their strongest decisions into one roadmap.

use_cases.title: Select an Implementation
use_cases.description: Produce several implementations, evaluate tests and quality metrics, then select or merge the strongest result.

use_cases.title: Build Debugging Consensus
use_cases.description: Collect independent root-cause hypotheses and proposed fixes, then document the most credible verified resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Create two plans for [feature]. Make one conservative and one delivery-focused. Compare risks, dependencies, and milestones. Produce one consolidated recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Implementation Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three implementations for [component] using the same interface and tests. Score correctness, readability, maintainability, performance, and security. Recommend one result.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Security-Weighted Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate plans from engineering, product, operations, and security perspectives. Consolidate them into phases. Give security extra weight and document every conflict.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Multi-Provider Reduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use approved providers to analyze [task]. Keep outputs separate and record attribution. Treat generated files as untrusted. Review all content before testing or consolidation.

output_examples.input: Create three plans for adding organization-level access controls.
output_examples.output: A consolidated roadmap presents phased delivery, an attribution table, unresolved tradeoffs, a risk matrix, and confidence for each major decision.

output_examples.input: Compare three implementations of a user service against one test suite.
output: The comparison ranks each implementation across five quality criteria.
The recommendation selects the strongest base and identifies useful traits from alternatives.
The report lists failed tests, required fixes, and the final destination.

output_examples.input: Gather several diagnoses for an intermittent authentication failure.
output_examples.output: A consensus report ranks root-cause hypotheses, cites supporting evidence, selects a minimal fix, and lists verification steps.

best_practices: Give every worker the same requirements, constraints, interfaces, and acceptance tests.
Keep provider outputs separate and preserve attribution before consolidation.
Review and sandbox generated code before compilation, tests, or file changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use more workers when their perspectives and instructions are identical.
Do not send secrets, private source, or regulated data to external providers.
Do not accept a reducer decision without checking evidence, conflicts, and failed validations.

faq.question: What does the MapReduce skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces separate worker artifacts and a consolidated plan, implementation comparison, review, or debugging resolution.

faq.question: Does it run multiple providers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents orchestration patterns. External CLIs and required agents must be installed, configured, and approved separately.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The package supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Its examples also mention Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode CLIs.

faq.question: How are competing outputs compared?
faq.answer: Reducers use weighted rubrics for plans, code, and debugging. They also record attribution, confidence, conflicts, and validation results.

faq.question: Can I use it with sensitive code?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review provider policies, remove secrets, obtain approval, and keep generated code inside an isolated test environment.

faq.question: Are all referenced workflow files included?
faq.answer: No. The package references reducer agent definitions and a debug consensus cookbook that are absent from the provided file structure.
